summary: A disciplined Phase 1. At 1440x900 the built page renders 1353.6x437.3 (aspect 3.0951, 94.0% of viewport), deck/keybed 0.540/0.444, all six section fractions within 0.006 of spec, 73 keys (43 white / 30 black) all inside the keybed at 0.610 black-key height, 131 named controls all reachable by the 5x5 elementFromPoint grid, and exactly two OLEDs. The voice is genuinely synthesized (discrete partials, -132.6 dB above 4 kHz, no audio asset in build/assets), and pointer, multi-touch, computer keyboard and Web MIDI each reach a full note lifecycle; velocity (RMS 0.0199 at vel 20 vs 0.1275 at vel 120), sustain from CC64 and space, 16-voice oldest-first stealing and blur all-notes-off all measure correct, and sweeping all 131 panel controls yields zero audio - nothing fakes success. Against that: loud 10-note chords clip (peak 1.21), MIDI disconnect leaves held voices sounding though the artifact claims otherwise, keys give no feedback for keyboard or MIDI notes, and at 390x844 only 38 of 131 controls stay pointer-reachable. All four gates reproduce on a clean install and rebuild to identical asset hashes.

criteria.label: Piano voice
evidence: Dependable and even across the assigned 73-key range: at MIDI velocity 100 the early-window RMS at the destination tap is 0.0954 (E1/28), 0.0967 (C4/60), 0.0845 (E7/100), and decay shortens with register exactly as artifact/src/audio/voice.ts intends (RMS 750 ms after onset: 0.0364 at E1 vs 0.0070 at E7). Note-on to first audible sample measured 49 ms (requestAnimationFrame-quantised upper bound).

Release behaves: a pointer-held C4 measures RMS 0.0828 while down and 0.0141 in the 400 ms window after release, reaching 0.0000 within about a second; a held C3 decays 0.0954 -> 0.0502 -> 0.0237 -> ... -> 0.0007 over 2.8 s.

Musically simplified in ways a player notices: the voice is six fixed sine partials (PARTIALS table in artifact/src/audio/voice.ts) scaled by one velGain scalar, so velocity changes loudness but not brightness, there is no hammer or key noise (measured -132.6 dB above 4 kHz), and the ring is far shorter than a real string.

Gain staging clips under heavy chords: measured destination peak 1.21 for a 10-note velocity-127 chord and 1.55 for 16 notes, versus a clean 0.87 for a 6-note velocity-110 chord. Master gain is a fixed 0.9 with no limiter or voice-count compensation (artifact/src/audio/web-audio-backend.ts).

criteria.label: Declared source honesty
evidence: The declared additive synthesis is confirmed by exercising the build rather than reading the declaration: a C3 sampled 120 ms after note-on shows discrete partials at 130.8/261.6/392.4/523.3 Hz at -43.8/-50.1/-55.3/-60.9 dB, harmonics 5-7 already at the -85.9 dB inter-partial floor, and nothing above 4 kHz (-132.6 dB). No broadband hammer noise or sample artefacts - this cannot be a recording.

build/assets contains exactly two files, index-6jOteH15.js and index-D1fSg7WE.css; no audio asset ships, matching sampleSources: [] and the single generatedSources entry synth-piano-basic in artifact/IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json.

Status text is truthful in both directions: normally "Piano voice: ready (synthesized piano)"; with window.AudioContext deleted it reads "Piano voice: Silent fallback - Silent fallback: Web Audio unavailable in this browser", and clicking a key then produces no audio and no page error (the label is duplicated in that string - cosmetic only).

criteria.label: Input coverage
evidence: All three required paths reach a full note lifecycle in the served build. Pointer: a real mouse press on key MIDI 60 gives RMS 0.0828 held and 0.0141 after mouse-up. Computer keyboard: 'q' gives RMS 0.0923, and a focused key button plus Enter gives 0.0950 falling to 0.0000 on release. Web MIDI: an injected navigator.requestMIDIAccess device sending 0x90 64 100 gives RMS 0.0889, status reads "MIDI: ready", and out-of-range notes 20 and 120 create zero buffer sources.

Independent multi-touch verified with CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent: two simultaneous touch points on MIDI 60 and 67 create 2 buffer sources and measure RMS 0.0975; lifting one point leaves 0.0494, so the other voice keeps sounding on its own.
MIDI failure modes are surfaced honestly: rejecting requestMIDIAccess yields "MIDI: denied" and a device statechange yields "MIDI: disconnected", each observed in the running build.

Coverage gaps a player would hit: KEY_TO_NOTE in artifact/src/input/keyboard-map.ts maps only 25 notes (C3-C5) with no octave shift, leaving 48 of the 73 keys unreachable from the computer keyboard, and no key highlights for computer-keyboard or MIDI notes (the background-image of key MIDI 60 is unchanged while 'q' or a MIDI note sounds; only a real mouse press changes it, through the CSS :active rule).

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle
evidence: Velocity maps in the right direction and by a musical amount: MIDI velocity 20 measures RMS 0.0199 versus 0.1275 at velocity 120; pointer strike position works too (top of key 0.0337, bottom of key 0.1358).

Sustain works from both available sources: 500 ms after note-off, RMS is 0.0000 with no pedal, 0.0251 with MIDI CC64 held and 0.0298 with the spacebar held; releasing the pedal drops it to 0.0000. Space still sustains while a panel button holds focus (0.0349), so it is not swallowed by focus.

Deterministic stealing and node cleanup: 16 held voices produce 0 stop() calls and the 17th produces exactly 1 (24 rapid notes -> 24 sources, 8 stops), matching MAX_VOICES 16 with oldest-released-then-oldest in artifact/src/audio/engine.ts. Two held notes at RMS 0.1235 fall to 0.0000 within 250 ms of a window blur, and a full probe session ends 39 sources against 38 stops.

One required cleanup trigger is missing: with a note held, firing the MIDI device disconnect leaves RMS 0.0483 afterwards versus 0.0488 in an identically timed control run with no disconnect - the voice is untouched and merely rings out, although the status line does correctly flip to "MIDI: disconnected".

criteria.label: Control feel & decorative boundary
evidence: The decorative boundary is exact, not approximate: sweeping all 131 [data-control-id] elements (focus, ArrowUp, and a click on every button) creates 0 new buffer sources, leaves RMS at 0.0000 and leaves the audio status string unchanged. Driving perf.masterLevel down to aria-valuenow 0 leaves a subsequent note at RMS 0.0943 (0.0889 at default) - it visibly moves and truthfully does nothing.

Controls report their state as they move: synth.filterCutoff goes 64 -> 127 over five PageUp presses (one per animation frame), Home 127 / End 0, then ArrowUp x3 -> 3, with the .knob-pointer transform rotating to match; a pointer drag on piano.level moves aria-valuenow 100 -> 49 with the fader cap at 14.66px and 3 of 8 LEDs lit; piano.type cycles Grand -> Upright -> Electric -> Clav with only the matching option LED lit.

Inertness is labelled rather than implied: the status bar reads "panel controls are decorative in Phase 1" and both OLEDs render "- phase 1: decorative -" / "- decorative -". Focus is visible (2px solid rgb(255,214,10) outline on the focused control).

Two state-reporting defects: every selector button reports aria-pressed="true" in all of its states (ButtonControl in artifact/src/components/controls.tsx forces pressed=true whenever options exist), and the key-down class is dead code - activeNotes is a ref, so the keybed never re-renders and only the CSS :active rule gives feedback, and only under a mouse.

criteria.label: Required Phase 1 controls present
evidence: The full Phase 1 surface is present and identifiable: 131 controls with data-control-id, every one carrying an aria-label, 52 role=slider controls all carrying aria-valuenow, all 131 reachable by the rubric's 5x5 elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900 with the page unscrolled, and exactly two OLEDs (Program and Synth), matching the visual spec's rule that these are the only primary displays.

Section landmarks from inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json are all rendered in their own section: nine drawbars plus LED level ladder, model and percussion switches in Organ; layer/level/type/model/timbre and the six detail switches in Piano; program OLED, dial, eight buttons, page nav, Live/Layer Scene, Store/Split and three morph assigns in Program; synth OLED with grouped osc/filter/dual-envelope/LFO-arp clusters; two effect groups plus Amp-EQ, Delay, Comp, Reverb and focus A/B in Effects; pitch stick, mod wheel, Master Level and STAGE 4 / NORD branding on exposed red chassis in Performance.

Two placement flaws against the reference: the Rotary Speaker block (speed, drive) is rendered inside the Organ section, whereas the visual spec explicitly places it on the exposed red chassis of the Performance band and says to score placement against the photograph; and in the desktop render the Piano and Synth clusters crowd, with the piano MODEL legend overlapping its type selector and the Organ level fader riding the section edge.

Coverage collapses at the narrow viewport: at 390x844 the same grid test finds only 38 of 131 controls reachable, with deck content overlapping and spilling toward the keybed, even though the chassis silhouette and all 73 keys survive.

criteria.label: Required piano feature IDs
evidence: All 11 Phase 1 feature IDs in artifact/tests/feature-matrix.json map to real, non-empty test files, and the suite reproduces on a clean install in a scratch copy: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile then test (11 files, 66 tests passed), typecheck, lint and build all pass, and the rebuild emits the same asset names as the published build (index-6jOteH15.js, index-D1fSg7WE.css), so build/ really is this source.

The behaviour behind those IDs is live in the build, not just in tests: note on/off and overlapping repeats (two note-ons on MIDI 60 create 2 sources; the first note-off leaves RMS 0.1246 and the second silences it), velocity, sustain from CC64 and space, 16-voice polyphony with stealing, blur all-notes-off, and a truthful ready/fallback/denied/disconnected status line.

One required piano input is only partly delivered: inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json requires sustain from a UI control, the keyboard mapping and MIDI CC64. Keyboard and CC64 both work, but there is no working on-screen pedal - piano.sustainPedal is a decorative routing button and does not engage sustain (part of the 131-control sweep that produced no audio).

criteria.label: Declared gaps are accurate
evidence: The central declarations hold up under measurement: the claim that every panel control is decorative and only keybed notes and sustain drive the engine is confirmed exactly by sweeping all 131 controls (0 buffer sources, RMS 0.0000, unchanged status); the 16-voice polyphony and oldest-first stealing claims match the measured 24 sources / 8 stops and the single steal on the 17th held note; the generated-not-recorded claim matches the spectrum; the labelled Silent fallback appears when Web Audio is removed.

One declaration is contradicted by the build. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json notes and the feature-matrix entry for piano.basic-status-cleanup both state that blur, disconnect and unmount stop every owned voice; a held note survives a MIDI device disconnect unchanged (RMS 0.0483 vs 0.0488 in the no-disconnect control). The candidate's own test named "MIDI disconnect stops owned voices and reports disconnected" only asserts the status string and then unmounts before checking voices.

Several real gaps are nowhere declared, while the Known deviations section of artifact/evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md lists only cosmetic ones: no working UI sustain control, a computer-keyboard map covering 25 of 73 notes with no octave shift, and no pressed-key feedback for computer-keyboard or MIDI notes.

The visual audit's narrow-viewport claim overstates the result: it says controls remain inspectable with no fixed clipping at 390x844, where 93 of 131 controls fail the elementFromPoint reachability grid and deck content visibly overlaps.

issues.title: MIDI disconnect does not stop owned voices, though the artifact claims it does
issues.detail: With a note held from an injected MIDI device, firing the device statechange leaves the voice untouched: RMS 0.0483 after the disconnect versus 0.0488 in an identically timed control run without one. The status line correctly flips to "MIDI: disconnected", but IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and tests/feature-matrix.json both assert that disconnect stops every owned voice, and the test bearing that name only checks the status string before unmounting. Impact is bounded because voices are finite 8 s buffers that ring out on their own, so no note is permanently stuck; the defect is the false claim plus the missing allNotesOff on statechange in artifact/src/App.tsx.

issues.title: Destination clipping on loud chords
issues.detail: Measured peak at the destination tap is 1.21 for a 10-note velocity-127 chord and 1.55 for 16 notes, both beyond the [-1,1] clamp, so a fortissimo chord distorts. A 6-note velocity-110 chord peaks at a clean 0.87. WebAudioBackend uses a fixed master gain of 0.9 with per-voice gain 1 and no limiter or voice-count compensation (artifact/src/audio/web-audio-backend.ts).

issues.title: Only 38 of 131 controls are pointer-reachable at 390x844
issues.detail: At the narrow viewport the whole instrument is scaled to 374x121 px, keeping its silhouette, aspect 3.0953 and all 73 keys, but the deck contents overlap and spill toward the keybed. The rubric's 5x5 elementFromPoint grid resolves only 38 of 131 controls to themselves or a descendant, versus 131 of 131 at 1440x900. artifact/evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md describes the same viewport as leaving controls inspectable with no clipping.

issues.title: Keys give no pressed feedback for computer-keyboard or MIDI notes
issues.detail: The key-down class in artifact/src/components/keybed.tsx is driven from the activeNotes ref, which never triggers a re-render, so it is never applied. Feedback comes only from the CSS :active rule, which fires for a real mouse press: the background-image of key MIDI 60 changes while the mouse holds it, but is unchanged while the same note sounds from 'q' or from MIDI.

issues.title: Selector buttons always report aria-pressed=true
issues.detail: ButtonControl in artifact/src/components/controls.tsx sets pressed = true whenever the control has options, so multi-state selectors such as piano.type, organ.model and fx.reverbType report aria-pressed="true" in every one of their states. Observed cycling piano.type through Grand, Upright, Electric and Clav: the option LED tracks correctly and data-option updates, but the exposed pressed state never changes, which misinforms assistive technology.

issues.title: No working UI sustain control
issues.detail: inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json requires sustain-pedal input from a UI control, the keyboard mapping and MIDI CC64. Space and CC64 both engage sustain (RMS 0.0298 and 0.0251 measured 500 ms after note-off, versus 0.0000 unpedalled), but no on-screen control does: piano.sustainPedal is a decorative routing button that produced no audio in the 131-control sweep.

issues.title: Rotary Speaker block placed in the Organ section rather than the Performance band
issues.detail: inputs/specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json lists rotary speaker controls among the Performance landmarks and notes that the block sits on the exposed red chassis below Master Level in reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg, to be scored against the photograph. The artifact renders organ.rotarySpeed and organ.rotaryDrive inside the Organ inset plate (artifact/src/components/sections.tsx), leaving the Performance band with only pitch stick, mod wheel, Master Level and branding.
